# WinVosk

> Offline dictation and voice-to-text for Windows: hold a hotkey, speak, and the
> recognised text is typed at the caret of the window you were typing in.
> Recognition runs locally with Vosk and a speech model; nothing leaves the
> machine. The language is the model's choice — Vosk publishes models for 32
> languages, and any model dropped into `models\` is picked up automatically. The
> model this repository is verified with is the small Russian one.

WinVosk is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Alpha Cephei
or the Vosk project. Vosk is a trademark of its owner, used here to name the
underlying toolkit.

## Read one of these

- [README.md](README.md) — what it is, how to install it, every setting, the
  vocabulary, and what to do when recognition is poor. Written for someone who has
  never seen the source.
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) — the verification bar, the invariants with the reason
  behind each one, and the release procedure. Read before changing code.
- [project.md](project.md) — the project context in one page: stack, layout,
  commands.
- [docs/HOWTO.md](docs/HOWTO.md) — the reference: internals, design rationale, the
  probes, the caveats.

Do not guess. Read the file the task names, use the pins in `requirements.txt`
unchanged, and verify with the project's own commands: `AGENTS.md` § Verification
lists them and says what each one proves. The models are published at
<https://alphacephei.com/vosk/models>, and README.md gives the archive URL and a
Hugging Face mirror that serves the same bytes.
